message.reasoning_content:

So I have solid primary data from Apple Newsroom and SEC 10-K. Decision: buy AAPL.

Thesis: FY24 revenue $391.0B (+2% YoY from $383.3B), Q4 revenue $94.9B +6% YoY (accelerating growth), net income $93.7B, diluted EPS $6.08 (down from $6.13 due to one-time $10.2B tax charge — so underlying earnings growth is better than headline), operating income $123.2B. Momentum improving into FY25 with Apple Intelligence rollout. Price $222.70.

Position sizing: mandate $10,000 per order max, $20,000 total today. Cash $50,000. Limit price close to market: $222.72 (ask) — that's ~0.01% above last. Use limit $223.00 maybe — "close to current market price". $223.00 is 0.13% above last. Fine. Let's use limit $222.90 (0.09% above). Quantity: 10000/222.90 = 44.86 → 44 shares = $9,807.60. Good.

Let's place 44 shares at limit $222.90.

Key figures: FY2024 revenue $391,035M USD millions; net income $93,736M; diluted EPS $6.08 USD/share; operating income $123,216M. Also Q4 revenue $94.9B — that's quarterly, fiscal_year 2024, unit USD billions. I'll include it as revenue 94.9 USD billions fiscal_year 2024? That could be confusing with annual revenue 391.035. Both are revenue FY2024 but different periods. Maybe safer to include the annual ones plus the quarterly as separate... The schema doesn't have a period field. I'll include annual figures and note quarterly separately in text. Actually I could include Q4 revenue 94.9 USD billions — but it might be read as conflicting with 391.035. I'll include only the annual figures to avoid ambiguity, plus mention quarterly in the summary text.

Actually, to be safe and complete, include annual revenue, net income, diluted EPS, operating income.
